issue.title: sase-core flake: sudo_runner post_spawn_identity_failure_reaps_barred_worker parses an empty worker.pid
issue.description:
Proposed by epic phase sase-157.9 (sase-core macOS portability epic) as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP; filed by the sase-157 land agent. Not caused by sase-157: the racy pattern is byte-identical at the epic's base commit (`60782f2^`, then `crates/sase_gateway/src/sudo_runner.rs:3232` and `:4297-4298`).

Repo: sase-core. Test: `crates/sase_gateway/src/sudo_runner/tests/worker.rs` `post_spawn_identity_failure_reaps_barred_worker` (~line 401). The same pattern exists in `post_spawn_publish_failure_reaps_barred_worker` (~line 442) and one other worker.pid read site in the same test module.

Observation (sase-157.9 note, 2026-09-21): panicked once with `ParseIntError { kind: Empty }` across repeated Linux `just check` runs under parallel load, and passed on rerun.

Root cause: `waiting_worker_script()` in `crates/sase_gateway/src/sudo_runner/tests/support.rs` records its pid with `printf '%s\n' "$$" > "$detach_dir/worker.pid"`. The shell opens and truncates the file before `printf` writes. The runner, on the forced identity/publish failure, reaps (kills) the barred worker. If the kill lands between the open and the write, `worker.pid` stays empty forever. The test then does `fs::read_to_string(...worker.pid)` and `pid.trim().parse::<u32>().unwrap()`, which panics on the empty string.

Fix (test-only): treat an empty `worker.pid` as "the worker never recorded its pid" in every read site (skip the liveness assertion, as the existing `if let Ok(...)` already does for a missing file), and/or have the stub write the pid atomically (`printf ... > "$f.tmp" && mv "$f.tmp" "$f"`). Keep the `!process_alive(pid)` assertion for the non-empty case. Verify with repeated `./scripts/check.sh test -p sase_gateway sudo_runner` runs under load.

The sase-core macOS CI leg is now required (sase-157.9), so this flake can turn master red on either platform.
